title: feat(cli): the console's frame-src names the storage origin a PDF preview frames, and nothing wider
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi92ncfFpPUpTD8314otX5oaG)_
Fixes #36443
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用 S3 类对象存储的部署上，控制台页面现在允许在对话框里内嵌显示存储桶上的 PDF，部署文档写明了存储桶要配的跨域规则；本地存储的部署用户无感。
- 为页内附件预览做准备（附件预览的服务端半边），替界面那张预览卡扫清浏览器安全策略的拦截。
- 若出错，最坏是 PDF 在页内显示不出来、只能新标签页打开；改动只放宽到存储桶这一个来源，可整体撤回。
- 要你做的：无。

## What changes

`packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts`, the Console document's content-security-policy:

- `frame-src` now names the storage origin beside `'self'` when the deployment stores files in S3 or an S3-compatible store. It is the one value `connect-src` already names for presigned uploads (`readStorageUploadOrigin`, read per document). The S3 adapter signs its download links (`getPresignedDownload`, behind `mintDownloadUrl`) with the same client options for the same bucket, so the signed `GET` the preview frames carries that origin; a test asserts the equality against real signed links.
- Nothing wider: never the operator's `OS_CONSOLE_CSP_CONNECT_SRC` hosts, never a scheme or wildcard. With local storage, or when the storage service cannot name its origin, `frame-src` is written exactly as before: absent (left to `default-src 'self'`), or `'self'` plus the Turnstile frame while that challenge is on. With Turnstile and S3 both on: `frame-src 'self' https://challenges.cloudflare.com STORE_ORIGIN`.
- The storage service's answer is now accepted only as an exact `http(s)` origin (it was any `connect-src` source shape). One value feeds both directives, so a scheme-only, wildcard, path or WebSocket answer is left out of both and reported once at `warn`. The adapters that ship answer `URL.origin`, so no deployment changes.
- The once-per-process warning for an unreadable storage origin now says a PDF preview cannot be framed (the new tab still works), and that `OS_CONSOLE_CSP_CONNECT_SRC` restores uploads only.

`content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`, after the "Uploads need S3" paragraph: the bucket CORS rule browser uploads and file previews need. `AllowedOrigins` is the Console's exact public origin, never `*`; `AllowedMethods` `GET`, `HEAD`, `PUT`; `AllowedHeaders` `content-type` (or `*`); `ExposeHeaders` `Content-Length`, `Content-Type`, `Content-Disposition`, `ETag`; `MaxAgeSeconds` `3000`. It says why a text or CSV preview needs the rule (a `GET` from the page) and a PDF frame does not, and that without it the preview falls back to opening the file in a new tab. The generated `content/docs/references/system/object-storage.mdx` is untouched.

Read first, by risk: `consoleContentSecurityPolicy` (the `frameSrc` block), `readStorageUploadOrigin` (the `STORAGE_ORIGIN` check), then the new `describe` in `console.content-security-policy.test.ts`.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit src/utils/console.content-security-policy.test.ts -t 'frame-src names the storage origin'` shows 11 passing cases.

## Tests

New top-level `describe` in the shared harness `src/utils/console.content-security-policy.test.ts` (real plugin, real Hono app, real `StorageServicePlugin`):

- local storage: no `frame-src`, `default-src 'self'`;
- R2: `frame-src` is exactly `'self'` plus the bucket origin;
- for four S3 shapes (R2 virtual-hosted, AWS regional, dotted bucket name, MinIO on `http://127.0.0.1:9000`): the extra source equals the origin of a real signed download link for a PDF;
- Turnstile plus S3: `'self'`, the Turnstile origin, the store origin, nothing more;
- `OS_CONSOLE_CSP_CONNECT_SRC` hosts (including a bare `https:`) never reach `frame-src`;
- a presigner that refuses the endpoint, and fake answers `https:`, `https://*.example.com`, a path, `wss:` and a number: neither directive widens, one warning.

## Acceptance notes

- The bucket CORS rule lives in the hand-written deployment page, not in `content/docs/references/system/object-storage.mdx`, which `build-docs.ts` generates and must not be hand-edited (surface amended on the card).
- Framing a PDF needs no bucket CORS (a frame navigation is not a CORS request); reading a text or CSV file from the page with a `GET` does, and so do the existing browser uploads (`PUT`).
- `StorageServicePluginOptions.s3` does not accept `forcePathStyle`, though `S3StorageAdapter` does; a path-style case was therefore dropped from the signed-link test. Observation only, not filed.
- Open #36518 answers stored bytes with a sandbox CSP and `nosniff` and keeps PDF inline. Measured in Chromium (below), a PDF served with that sandbox header still mounts the browser's PDF viewer inside the frame.

## Verification

<details><summary>Real Chromium: a cross-origin PDF in an iframe, before and after the frame-src change</summary>

```
before | csp frame-src: (none) | store requests: 0 | frames: ["http://localhost:34597/","chrome-error://chromewebdata/"]
after  | csp frame-src: frame-src 'self' http://127.0.0.1:37259 | store requests: 2 | frames: [..., "http://127.0.0.1:37259/c.pdf","chrome-extension://mhjfbmdgcfjbbpaeojofohoefgiehjai/index.html", ...]
with the sandbox CSP of #36518 on the PDF response, after: same frames, the PDF viewer extension mounts
```
</details>
